bull.t: Debt-free balance sheet & pro forma cash runway
bull.b: A debt-free balance sheet and ~$535M pro forma cash materially increase Altimmune’s ability to fund global Phase III start‑up and multi-year trials without immediate dilutive financing. This financial flexibility supports longer-term execution, CRO commitments, and clinical supply obligations through registrational milestones.

Breakthrough Therapy designation and alignment with FDA/EMA on PERFORMA protocol de‑risks regulatory pathway, enables more frequent regulator engagement, and can accelerate review timelines. This structural recognition raises the program’s probability of efficient development and potential expedited access if trials confirm benefit.

bull.t: Positive Phase II signals across indications
bull.b: Robust Phase II efficacy and tolerability in RECLAIM (AUD) plus prior IMPACT MASH signals strengthen pemvidutide’s value proposition across metabolic and liver indications. Consistent biomarker and clinical endpoints improve confidence in translatability to registrational studies and increase partnership and label expansion optionality.

bear.t: Persistent cash burn and weak cash generation
bear.b: Ongoing negative operating and free cash flow create structural reliance on capital markets or partnerships until commercial revenue emerges. Despite pro forma proceeds, sustained development costs for multi‑year Phase III programs mean dilution or new funding rounds remain likely if timelines extend or additional programs are pursued.

bear.t: Long Phase III timelines to registrational readout
bear.b: A 52‑week biopsy primary endpoint and a multi‑year global Phase III create an extended horizon to potential approval and revenue, raising execution risk and capital consumption over time. Long timelines magnify the impact of operational setbacks and allow competitors more opportunity to capture market share before launch.

A crowded GLP‑1/dual‑ and triple‑agonist field heightens the need for clear clinical differentiation on tolerability and liver efficacy. Competitive entrants with established brands or broader efficacy could limit market share and pricing power, requiring stronger post‑approval evidence or strategic partnerships to secure commercial success.
